Materials and crafting

The formulas below describe this engine's current rules. Item and spell examples are calculated from your loaded game data.

Which material should I choose?

Choose the material on an item page to compare its finished statistics. For enchantments, check rune slots and charge capacity before cost: an affordable material may not support your spell. Add the finished item to a plan to collect the required materials.

Why is this enchantment unavailable?

The spell must fit the item's slots and charge capacity. Weapons and armour also need an item-enchantment rune. The constructor reports incompatible combinations; fixed story items are not crafting recipes.

A recipe accepts materials of its authored material type. Each listed material variant is built with the same item calculations used by the inventory and shops.

Weight = prototype weight × material weight multiplier. Durability = prototype durability × material durability multiplier. Value = prototype value + component count × material value. Charge capacity and rune slots combine prototype and material values.

The blueprint view lists the component count. The material selector shows completed variants on the same item page. Material pages show multipliers and link to compatible items. Shop buy, sell and repair prices can differ from the base value.
